author: CyberShield project
description: Defensive YARA rules written for this project. These rules detect phishing artefacts, credential-theft behaviour, droppers, ransomware notes, coin-mining configurations, persistence mechanisms and anti-analysis evasion. They are intentionally behavioural rather than signature-bound so that they remain useful as attackers change tooling.

severity_policy.note: A rule tagged 'authoritative' produces a finding that raises the risk-score floor. Only use this tag where the match is by itself decisive.

changes: Added ransomware note, banking web-inject and C2-tunnelling rule sets.
Split financial-theft behaviours out of the general malware rules.
Added encoded-payload, PowerShell download-and-execute and Office macro auto-execute rules.
Removed two rules that produced false positives on legitimate installer scripts.
Initial rule set: document lures, obfuscated loaders, droppers, browser credential theft.

testing.note: Every rule is exercised by backend/tests/test_yara_rules.py using benign corpora, which must produce no matches. A rule that cannot be made to pass that check is not shipped.
